Review\n`doas zsh OPENBSD/OPERATOR.sh --plan` before a mirror-only change; routine\napplication releases use the workstation operator and pinned deployment path.\n\nHands-off: workstation preflight + serial Rails CI + asset build/attestation →\npin SHA → stage production artifacts → `tmux` session `pub5-deploy` on vm23\n→ `vps-deploy` as **root** (git still as `dev`) → workstation collector streams\ntmux's in-memory pane into `~/.pub5/deployments/deploy-*.log` → local\n`vps-state` + public canary → redacted, expiring paste. The workstation capture\nprocess is detached from the terminal, so an SSH or terminal disconnect does\nnot stop the collector while the workstation remains running. vm23 writes no\ndeploy transcript: only structured recovery receipts remain under\n`/var/db/pub5/deploy_runs`.\n\nA direct natural-language instruction to deploy **OPENBSD + all RAILS apps + MASTER/web\nto vm23** is an explicit execution request; the equivalent shorthand **“redeploy\neverything on vm23”** resolves to every active registered deployment surface (the\ntracked OpenBSD mirror plus the complete app inventory, including MASTER/web). It\ndoes not mean every repository file or arbitrary host path. These explicit full-scope\nrequests do not require a separate written plan or a second confirmation prompt.\nThe normal local preflight, pinned revision, mirror/manual admission gate, serial\nproduction rollout, health checks and canary remain mandatory. A plan-only request\nis conversational and cannot start a deploy. Requests with explicit exclusions and\npartial or model-classified app/group requests retain the `/deploy --confirm` review\ngate. Never run `/fix` on vm23.\nAttach: `tmux attach -t pub5-deploy`.\n\n## What a full deployment actually applies\n\nThe `all` target is the combined release path, not just the Rails fleet:\n\n1. The workstation proves and pins one commit; vm23 checks that exact SHA before any service is stopped.\n2. The remote `vps-deploy all` applies the tracked filesystem mirror by invoking `zsh OPENBSD/OPERATOR.sh --apply`.\n3. The mirror installer validates native configs and NSD zones, backs up changed files and the managed root crontab, installs each file with its declared owner and mode, verifies read-back, and activates only affected services. SSH configuration remains protected; doas changes require the separate guarded path.\n4. The application inventory is deployed serially, with bounded health checks, recovery of services that were up before the run, and post-deploy canaries.\n\nThe pinned checkout is the whole pub5 repository, so the same release also\nadvances all tracked STUDIO source under `/home/dev/pub5/STUDIO`. STUDIO is\nsource and local creative tooling (Dilla, LoRA, Postpro and the Studio CLI),\nnot a registered vm23 service: it is not installed as a daemon or exposed as\na separate deploy target. For a full `all` release, workstation preflight\nsyntax-checks STUDIO and runs `rake -f replicate/Rakefile check test` before\nany SSH or production change. A dirty or untracked file in any of MASTER,\nRAILS, OPENBSD or STUDIO blocks the release, so the pinned commit cannot\nsilently omit local STUDIO edits.\n\nThis is the controlled equivalent of copying the mirror into `/`, not a blind recursive copy. It deliberately does not reboot the host: the installer restarts the affected daemons/services after validation. A reboot is a separate maintenance decision, not an automatic side effect of every release.\n\nFor a mirror-only operation, inspect first with `doas zsh OPENBSD/OPERATOR.sh --plan`; apply only after review with `doas zsh OPENBSD/OPERATOR.sh --apply`; verify with `doas zsh OPENBSD/OPERATOR.sh --verify`. A full `vps-deploy all` already runs the apply step as part of its pinned release.\n\n## Deployment transcripts and paste sharing\n\nDeployment transcripts live on the operator workstation, not vm23:\n\n- `~/.pub5/deployments/deploy-*.log`, directory mode `0700`, file mode `0600`.\n- Each completed deploy publishes a redacted engineering transcript using\n  MASTER's existing paste publisher. The preferred paste expires after one day;\n  the fallback expires after seven days. The paste URL and publication result\n  are appended to the local transcript.\n- Credentials, private-key blocks, authorization headers, cookies, URL\n  credentials, tokens and email addresses are redacted before publication.\n  `MASTER_LOG_PUBLISH=0` disables paste publication without disabling local\n  logging.\n- OpenSSH transport diagnostics remain local at\n  `~/.pub5/ssh-connections.log`.\n\nOn vm23, `vps-deploy` writes only the bounded recovery receipts under\n`/var/db/pub5/deploy_runs`. Its receipt stores a `local://deploys/...`\nreference, not a remote log path. Remote tmux scrollback is an in-memory\ntransport buffer and is removed after the workstation collector receives the\nterminal exit marker. It is not a durable log store.\n\n`newsyslog(8)` continues to rotate the system and host-service logs in the\nOpenBSD mirror. It no longer has rules for deploy transcripts because those\nfiles are not written on vm23.\n\n## Repo layout\n\n`MASTER/`, `RAILS/`, `OPENBSD/`, `STUDIO/` at the repo root, plus dotfolders. `MASTER/tools/` is inside MASTER and keeps compatibility entrypoints.\nCanonical inventories: `RAILS/apps.yml`, `OPENBSD/deploy_inventory.json`. The\nJSON is generated from `apps.yml` by `ruby OPENBSD/bin/sync_deploy_inventory.rb`,\nand the `domain_alignment` check fails when the two disagree. Deploy\nchecks (`integrity_check.rb`, `verify_deploy_identity.rb`,\n`deploy_inventory.json`) live at `OPENBSD/` top level, and so does\nOld quarantine samples were deliberately removed from the tracked tree. The\nretired `manual_master_deploy.ksh` is not a recovery route; it refuses to run.\n`bin/dr-pull` recovers databases. There is no `archive/`; git history holds\nthe old installers.\n\n## Deployment map\n\n```text\nInternet\n  -> pf\n  -> relayd TLS/SNI\n  -> loopback app ports\n      -> MASTER Falcon on ai.brgen.no\n      -> brgen Rails app and vertical subdomains\n      -> amber Rails app\n      -> bsdports Rails app\n  -> NSD/acme/httpd for DNS and certificate plumbing\n```\n\nRuntime contract: TLS terminates at relayd; apps listen on loopback-only ports;\nRails uses SQLite plus Solid Queue/Cache; secrets live in `/etc/*.env`; source\nof truth on the VPS is `/home/dev/pub5`; long deploys run under tmux.\n\nHTTP serving is intentionally narrower: `httpd` listens on port 80 solely for\n`/.well-known/acme-challenge/*` (HTTP-01). It does not redirect ordinary\nrequests, host static sites or terminate TLS. `acme-client` writes challenge\nfiles under `/var/www/acme`; certificate renewal restarts `relayd` only when a\ncertificate actually changes. `relayd` terminates TLS on port 443 and forwards\nall application traffic to the registered Falcon loopback services. The former\nlocalhost Postpro static-photo preview on port 6666 is retired; Postpro itself\nremains a local processing tool.\n\nCheck flow — workstation: `OPENBSD/bin/check` → `verify_deploy_identity` → Rails\nproduction/domain/phantom/frontend checks → OpenBSD deploy smoke. Release:\n`MASTER/bin/operator vps deploy <app|group|all> --remote` runs workstation\npreflight, selected Rails `bin/ci` suites and asset builds, pins one SHA, then\nstages and deploys that exact release on vm23. The host performs bounded sync,\nattestation checks, read-only production-bundle verification, service operations\nand loopback health checks. Finish with the workstation public canary. Never run\n`git pull`, Rails test suites, bundle installation or asset precompilation on vm23.\n\n## Privileged deploy boundary\n\nThe host has no command broker. Ordinary privileged operations use OpenBSD's\nnative commands under the single `:wheel as root` doas rule in\n`OPENBSD/mirror/etc/doas.conf`. The rule has no `keepenv`; only the measured\n`setenv` allowlist crosses the boundary. `OPERATOR.sh` installs the policy only\nthrough `validate_doas.ksh`, which checks both the root path and the allowlisted\nvariables and restores the previous file on failure.\n\n`OPERATOR.sh` also installs the fixed app-user helpers from the tracked mirror:\n\n- `usr/local/libexec/ci-prepare.ksh` verifies app paths and grants checkout-read\n  group access.\n- `usr/local/libexec/ci-sync.ksh` stages tracked `HEAD` paths as the app user.\n- App `bin/ci` runs on the workstation; vm23 refuses CI execution.\n- The retired `ci-run.ksh` helper is a refusal stub.\n- `usr/local/libexec/rails-task.ksh` exposes read-only bundle checks and\n  essential database tasks, then drops to the app user.\n- `usr/local/libexec/rails-sync.ksh` syncs the production tree as the app user\n  and preserves runtime state.\n\n`vps-deploy` controls services with `/usr/sbin/rcctl` as root. It writes durable\nfleet receipts through `OPENBSD/lib/deploy_records.rb` to the root-private\n`/var/db/pub5/deploy_runs/` directory. Receipt writes are inventory-derived,\natomic and readable as `root:wheel` mode `0640`; the pinned commit, original\nservice snapshot, port map, restore order and last stage are retained for\ninterrupted-run diagnosis. `vps-state` reads the same records directly and uses\nnative `rcctl` for service state. `vps_ci.sh` writes its per-app stamp with a\nnative atomic Ruby write.\n\n`SECRET_KEY_BASE` is read or created by `RAILS/_database.sh` with an atomic\n`File.link` write; it crosses only in the child environment, never in the shell\ncommand text. Bundle directories and caches are app-owned. `relayd` route\nverification is read-only: it checks the installed root-owned\n`/etc/relayd.conf`, the TLS keypair and the app backend/port. New hostnames must\nbe added to `OPENBSD/mirror/etc/relayd.conf` in a deliberate `OPERATOR.sh`\nchange first. `deploy-smoke` and `vps_install_all.sh` use native `rcctl`.\n\nThe retired `pub5-admin` program and manual page are not tracked. Do not restore\nthem. The active deployer, helpers, doas policy, mirror, tests, safety check and\nrecovery paths all use the native boundary above. Keep the `doas.conf` and wheel\nmembership unchanged until the focused and full OpenBSD contract suites pass;\nnarrow the `dev` rule only in a separately reviewed rollout with an authenticated\noperator recovery path established first.\n\n## Command selection and diagnosis\n\n### Mandatory full-source and full-manual preflight\n\nThis gate covers **every file under `OPENBSD/`** and every OpenBSD-native\ncommand, tool, daemon and configuration interface. It is not limited to\n`rc`, `rcctl`, or configuration files under `etc/`.\n\nBefore editing any file in this tree, read the entire current file and the\nrelevant dependencies, callers, consumers, generators, schemas and tests.\nBefore invoking or relying on an OpenBSD-native interface, read the complete\nmanual pages for the exact target release and architecture:\n\n- every native command/tool the operation will invoke;\n- each configuration-file format/interface it reads or changes;\n- the owning daemon/service and its lifecycle/control interface;\n- the validation, reload, restart, update or recovery tools involved;\n- all relevant `SEE ALSO` pages needed to understand the interface.\n\nThe target release's own pages are the ones that count: current-manual pages are not proof for an older host.\n\nThis applies across boot and init, services, accounts, permissions, storage,\nfilesystems, packages, patching, kernel/sysctl, devices, networking, PF, DNS,\nNSD, relayd, TLS/certificates, cron, logging, monitoring, backup and recovery.\nThose examples are illustrative, not a finite list. It applies to shell/ksh,\nRuby, service scripts, config, data, checks, tests, installers, documentation\nand generated inputs. A prose/data file with no native interface still needs\ncomplete source and schema/contract review; do not invent irrelevant manuals.\n\n1. Establish the target host, OS release and architecture from authoritative\n   inventory or a minimal read-only identity probe. Record hostname,\n   `uname -srm`, `uname -v` and relevant PATH entries. Do not dump secrets.\n2. Read each required page in full, including all sections; a synopsis,\n   `man -k` result, search excerpt or remembered behavior is not a read.\n   On the target, use the native manual reader with a non-interactive pager\n   such as `man -P cat <section> <page>`. Follow relevant `SEE ALSO`\n   references until the tool, file format and service lifecycle are clear.\n3. Record one receipt per page: host, OS release, architecture, canonical\n   page and section, source (target-local manual or exact release-versioned\n   manual URL), SHA-256 of the full rendered text, byte count, line count and\n   `complete=true`. The full content must be available for inspection;\n   a hash alone does not prove it was read.\n4. If a page is missing, mismatched, partial, truncated or unverifiable,\n   report BLOCKED. Do not invoke the native tool, operate the daemon, edit\n   the file or continue with dependent operations. Do not substitute current\n   manuals for an older target release or training-data assumptions. When\n   the target manual is unavailable locally, use only the exact release page\n   at `https://man.openbsd.org/OpenBSD-<release>/<page>`, and cite that\n   release; a current-manual URL is not equivalent.\n\nThe manual-reading interface itself and the minimum read-only identity probe\nneeded to establish an unknown target are the only preflight exceptions.\n\n**Executable admission gate.** An OPENBSD task contract carries\n`openbsd_preflight`: hostname, exact release, architecture, the in-scope\nOPENBSD paths, full current source reads for the target and reviewed\ndependencies/callers, and one content-bearing receipt per native manual\ninterface. Every source receipt binds its current repository bytes by SHA-256,\nbyte and line count. Every manual receipt retains the complete text, canonical\npage/section, exact-release or target-local source, SHA-256, byte count, line\ncount and `complete=true`. A prose/data file with no native interface needs\nan explicit evidence-based reason instead of fabricated manual pages.\n\nThe same receipt is checked by Fix::WriteGuard, the Fold Constitution and the\ncommand Shell. Missing, stale, out-of-scope or incomplete evidence blocks the\nwrite or operation before it is performed. Source edits invalidate receipts\nfor any reviewed source they change; rebuild the preflight before proceeding.\n\nFor a full `vps-deploy all` operation, the admission gate also inventories every\ntracked configuration source in `OPENBSD/mirror/etc/`, `OPENBSD/mirror/var/nsd/`\n(including every zone file), and the mirrored mail-client dotfiles. It derives a\nper-file report joining source-read digests to the exact-release manual receipts\nfor each mapped interface. Any unmapped format, missing source read, stale source,\nor missing manual receipt blocks the deploy. The intentionally inert\n`etc/litestream.yml` still requires a complete source read, but no fictitious\nOpenBSD manual is assigned to an uninstalled daemon.\nThe report is retained locally at\n`MASTER/.master/openbsd_mirror_coverage.json`; it includes the target identity,\nper-file status, source SHA-256 values and each required manual-page receipt.\nThe only bootstrap commands are the manual reader and the minimum read-only\nidentity probe. This is an admission requirement, not a claim that a remote\nhost has been inspected when no host evidence was supplied.\n\n**Receipt hand-off for an interactive /fix.** The first contract is created\nbefore the agent has read the target, so it deliberately contains no preflight.\nThe agent may read source and manuals without write permission. After completing\nthat read, it writes MASTER/.master/openbsd_preflight.json (ignored runtime\nstate, never committed) with this envelope:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"head_sha\": \"the exact 40-character output of git rev-parse HEAD\",\n  \"created_at\": \"UTC ISO-8601 timestamp\",\n  \"openbsd_preflight\": {\n    \"hostname\": \"vm23\",\n    \"os_release\": \"7.8\",\n    \"architecture\": \"amd64\",\n    \"scope\": [\"OPENBSD/**\"],\n    \"source_reads\": [\n      {\"path\": \"OPENBSD/mirror/etc/rc.conf\", \"content\": \"complete exact file content\", \"complete\": true}\n    ],\n    \"native_interfaces\": [\"rcctl(8)\", \"rc.conf(5)\", \"rc.d(8)\"],\n    \"manual_pages\": [\n      {\n        \"page\": \"rcctl\",\n        \"section\": \"8\",\n        \"source\": \"https://man.openbsd.org/OpenBSD-7.8/rcctl.8\",\n        \"content\": \"complete manual output, not synopsis or excerpt\",\n        \"complete\": true\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\nInclude every target/dependency source file and every applicable command,\nconfiguration-format, owning-daemon, lifecycle, validation and recovery manual.\nUse the exact target release in every versioned manual URL; the title in the\nfirst eight lines must identify the requested page and section. The runtime\nhydrates this receipt into the active TaskContract only when HEAD matches and\nthe receipt is no more than one hour old. Every source is re-hashed at admission.\nIf the file is absent, malformed, stale or outside scope, the operation remains\nBLOCKED. Rebuild it after a source edit or a target release/architecture change.\n\nFor example, a PF change requires the full target-release `pfctl(8)` and\n`pf.conf(5)` pages plus relevant network/anchor pages; an NSD change needs\nthe relevant `nsd(8)`, `nsd.conf(5)`, zone-format and reload pages; a package\nchange needs the package tools and package-specific documentation. Apply the\nsame dependency-driven rule to every native interface; these examples do not\nlimit it.\n\nThe target host determines command semantics. Begin with bounded, read-only\nidentity facts only, then satisfy the preflight above before using other\nutilities. Never assume Linux `/proc`, GNU-only flags, or an optional package\nexists on the host.\n\nFor a daemon incident, distinguish configured, enabled, running, locally healthy,\nand publicly reachable. Check the relevant `rcctl configtest` and `rcctl check`,\nthen inspect the process, listening socket, and service logs. For a public outage,\ntrace DNS and TLS, PF and relayd/httpd, the loopback listener, and the application\nin that order. A healthy TLS endpoint alone does not prove the backend is up;\na failed immediate service check during startup does not by itself prove a crash.\nVerify independently with a service signal, an application-level request, and\nthe actual public route where relevant.\n\nFor patch state, `syspatch -c` lists available base patches and\n`syspatch -l` lists installed patches. Neither alone decides a release upgrade.\nRead the target release's upgrade instructions, establish a usable backup and\nconsole/recovery path, and assess service and package compatibility before\nproposing an upgrade.\nOpenBSD supports upgrades only to the immediately following release. If the host\nis more than one release behind the target, plan and verify each supported\ntransition in sequence; never assume a direct jump is supported.\n\nBefore any mutation, preserve the observed state and establish a recovery route.\nValidate configuration with the service's supported test (for example,\n`rcctl configtest` or `pfctl -nf /etc/pf.conf`), make one scoped change, and\nverify its effect independently. Do not infer success from a wrapper's exit code\nwhen the underlying operation has its own receipt or health check.\n\n## SSH\n\nPF has an explicit, unthrottled quick-pass rule for TCP port 22. There is no\ndynamic brute-force table, automatic source ban, or global state flush. HTTP,\nHTTPS and SMTP limits are local to their own service rules and cannot remove SSH\nstates. SSH remains key-only with root login and password authentication disabled.\n\n| Target | Command |\n|--------|---------|\n| VM (apps) | `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_brgen dev@brgen.no` or `ssh brgen` |\n| VMM host | `ssh -p 31415 -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_brgen dev@server4.openbsd.amsterdam` |\n| Console | `vmctl console vm23` |\n\nSSH aliases, host topology and provider access are kept in this runbook so live-operation guidance has one source.\n\n## Domains\n\n| Service | URL |\n|---------|-----|\n| MASTER | `https://ai.brgen.no` |\n| brgen | `https://brgen.no` |\n| brgen · marketplace | `https://markedsplass.brgen.no` |\n| brgen · dating | `https://dating.brgen.no` |\n| brgen · playlist | `https://radio.brgen.no` (canonical), `https://playlist.brgen.no` (second host, restored 2026-11-19; DNS record and acme SAN from BOOTSTRAP.sh ALL_DOMAINS, relayd route beside radio's, app-side alias in `Brgen::DomainRegistry::RADIO_SUBDOMAINS`) |\n| brgen · takeaway | `https://takeaway.brgen.no` |\n| brgen · tv | `https://tv.brgen.no` |\n| brgen · messenger | `https://messenger.brgen.no` |\n| amber | `https://amberapp.art` |\n| bsdports | `https://bsdports.org` |\n| mrdamascy (demo) | `https://mrd.brgen.no` |\n\nThe brgen verticals (marketplace/dating/playlist/takeaway/tv/messenger + `maps`)\nare one Rails app served under subdomains via `<brgen>`; relayd already routes\nthem all (`etc/relayd.conf`).\n\n### Bringing a domain up\n\nSeven city domains serve brgen, each scoped to its own city: `brgen.no`,\n`oshlo.no`, `trndheim.no`, `stvanger.no`, `cardff.uk`, `edinbrgh.uk`,\n`frankfrt.de`. Six more hold a zone that nsd serves and an `acme-client.conf` block, and\nnone has an NS record at its registrar, so nothing asks our nameserver for\nthem. Registry lookups on 2026-10-12 found only `brssels.be` registered.\n`brmingham.uk`, `glasgw.uk`, `lverpool.uk` and `mnchester.uk` (Nominet,\n\"This domain name has not been registered\", after \"Renewal required\" in\nJune) and `dnver.us` are unregistered: the .uk names lapsed on 24 and 25 June\n2026 and anyone may now register them. Bringing one up starts with buying it\nback, which is a registrar login, or with deleting its zone and\n`acme-client.conf` block if the city is dropped (record that in\n`data/domain_released.yml`). `ruby OPENBSD/bin/domain_watch.rb` is the check.\n\nThe order below is not a preference. Each step needs the one above it, and the\nlast step is the one that bites: relayd refuses to start when a `tls keypair`\nnames a certificate that is not on disk, so adding the keypair early takes down\nevery site relayd serves, not just the new one.\n\n1. **Delegate at the registrar** — NS to `ns.hyp.net` and `ns.brgen.no`,\n   matching `oshlo.no`. This is the only step that is not on this box.\n2. **Confirm it resolves to us**, or acme cannot answer its own challenge: `ruby\n   -rresolv -e 'puts Resolv.getaddress(\"glasgw.uk\")'` → `46.23.89.226`.\n3. **Issue the certificate.** The `domain` block already exists in\n   `/etc/acme-client.conf`; `doas /usr/local/bin/renew-certs.sh` picks it up, or\n   `doas acme-client -v glasgw.uk` for one.\n4. **Check the certificate is on disk** before touching relayd: `doas ls -l\n   /etc/ssl/glasgw.uk.fullchain.pem`.\n5. **Add `tls keypair \"glasgw.uk\"`** to `etc/relayd.conf` beside the other city\n   keypairs, then `doas relayd -n` and only then `doas rcctl reload relayd`.\n6. **Verify**: `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://glasgw.uk/` is\n   200, and the page title names the city.\n\nThe stack serves three Rails apps (brgen, amber, bsdports) plus MASTER. `baibl`,\n`blognet` and `hjerterom` are retired; on 2026-08-12 their users, home\ndirectories (1.6 GB between them), rc.d scripts, `/etc/*.env` files, login\nclasses, certificate symlinks and DNS zones were removed from vm23, and their\nown domains (`baibl.no`, `blognet.no`, `hjerterom.no`) with them. Databases are\nkept at `/var/backups/pub4/{hjerterom,deleted-apps}-20260812`. `foodielicio.us`\nand the `anti{casino,gambling,betting}blog.com` trio were not removed: they stay\nin `data/dns.yml`'s `extra_zones`, and nsd still serves them.\n\nThe repo recorded baibl and blognet as removed two months before the box lost\nthem, which is why `port_inventory` scans the config files where that kind of\nresidue lives, so the next removal cannot be half-done quietly.\n\nSeven city apexes serve as of 2026-08-12\n(`Brgen::DomainRegistry::LIVE_DOMAINS`); the rest of `ENTRIES` is either\nNXDOMAIN at the registrar or parked at Domeneshop.\n\nTLS terminates at relayd. Rails sets `config.assume_ssl = true`; do not enable\n`force_ssl`.\n\n### NSD and DNSSEC\n\nThe committed `OPENBSD/mirror/var/nsd/etc/nsd.conf` and\n`OPENBSD/mirror/var/nsd/zones/master/*.zone` files are the pregenerated\nproduction payload. Normal deploy applies these files literally; it does not run\nthe generator. The single `MASTER/bin/operator vps deploy all --remote` path\nvalidates the source zones, backs up current signed zones, signs every zone using\nits already-active KSK/ZSK set, validates every resulting `.zone.signed` file,\nthen reloads or restarts NSD. A missing or ambiguous key pair fails the release\nbefore NSD activation.\n\nA signing success is not a public DNSSEC validation result. A validating\nresolver also needs the parent zone to publish a DS record matching the active\nKSK. `OPENBSD/bin/ds-records` derives DS records from the DNSKEYs in the signed\nzone. Publish only for domains that are registered and delegated to this\nnameserver; never publish DS for a parked, unregistered or differently\ndelegated domain. Verify with a validating resolver (for example\n`delv <domain> SOA`) and require a validated answer.\n\nRoutine signing preserves the DNSKEY set already published by each signed zone.\nA new key appearing on disk is not automatically adopted. KSK rollover requires\npublishing the new DNSKEY, adding its DS at the parent, waiting the parent DS\nTTL/propagation interval, and only then retiring the old KSK. The private keys\nmust be backed up off-host in encrypted storage and a restore verified before\nany DS publication or key change.\n\n### Mr. Damascy demo\n\n`https://mrd.brgen.no` serves RAILS/mrdamascy, the restaurant's ordering PWA, as\na demo for its owner. It is an ordinary inventory app (apps.yml port 47314,\n`rc.d/mrdamascy`, `vps-deploy mrdamascy`) kept deliberately light: production\nuses Falcon's tracked `RAILS/mrdamascy/falcon.rb` host configuration and\n`preload.rb`, one loopback-only worker with a three-connection Active Record\npool, SQLite under `/home/mrdamascy/app/storage`, no jobs\nworker (the app enqueues none), and Vipps, Stripe and Wolt in mock mode, so no\npayment key exists on the box. `mrd` is an A record in the brgen.no zone and a\nSAN on the brgen.no certificate; `/etc/ssl/mrd.brgen.no.crt` and\n`/etc/ssl/private/mrd.brgen.no.key` are symlinks to the brgen.no pair, the same\narrangement as ai.brgen.no. resource_guard does not know it, so it is never shed;\nunder pressure the guard sheds bsdports and amber instead.\n\nThe menu comes from `db/seeds.rb`, which destroys and recreates every row,\norders and users included. It ran once at first deploy; a deploy never seeds,\nso run it again only to reset the demo:\n\n```zsh\ndoas /usr/local/libexec/rails-task.ksh mrdamascy db-seed\n```\n\n**Stop the demo** (reversible; the tree, database and certificate stay):\n\n```zsh\ndoas rcctl stop mrdamascy\ndoas rcctl disable mrdamascy\n```\n\n`disable` takes it out of `pkg_scripts`, so a reboot does not start it.\n\nrelayd then marks `<mrdamascy>` down and mrd.brgen.no answers TLS with an empty\nreply. Start it again with `doas rcctl enable mrdamascy && doas rcctl start mrdamascy`.\n\n**Remove the route as well**, so mrd.brgen.no stops terminating at all. Every\nmrdamascy line in relayd.conf names `mrdamascy` or `mrd.brgen.no`:\n\n```zsh\ndoas cp -p /etc/relayd.conf /etc/relayd.conf.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M)\ndoas ruby34 -e 'f = \"/etc/relayd.conf\"; File.write(f, File.readlines(f).reject { |l| l.match?(/mrdamascy|mrd\\.brgen\\.no/) }.join)'\ndoas relayd -n -f /etc/relayd.conf && doas rcctl restart relayd\n```\n\nThen in the repo: put `deployed: false` back on mrdamascy in RAILS/apps.yml\n(drop its `domain` and `deploy_script`), run `ruby OPENBSD/bin/sync_deploy_inventory.rb`,\ntake `mrd` out of `extra_hosts` and `cert_extra_names` in `OPENBSD/data/dns.yml`,\nrun `ruby OPENBSD/bin/render_dns.rb`, and remove the same lines from\n`OPENBSD/mirror/etc/relayd.conf`, so the tree matches the box. The DNS record and the\nSAN can stay until the next certificate renewal; neither serves anything.\n\n## Agent contract\n\nModes: local contributor (edit repository files and run local checks; do not SSH),\nworkstation release operator (run preflight, selected Rails CI and asset builds;\nstart one pinned remote deployment at a time), and recovery (human-directed console\nor resource guard only to restore access or health, then document the fix).\n\n**Hard stops — AI agents must not autonomously:**\n\n| Action | Why |\n|--------|-----|\n| `vmctl console/stop/start/reboot` on server4 | Serial console sessions have caused VM reboots and site outages |\n| `pkill`/`kill` of `cu`, `vmctl`, or other VMM console sessions on server4 | Disrupts other operators and can wedge vm23 |\n| `vps_console.exp` without human approval | Gated by `I_UNDERSTAND_CONSOLE_RISK=1`; recovery-only |\n| Deploy, install, or `pkill` deploy workers from the serial console | Bypasses SSH safety, tmux, and load checks |\n| Target vm27 or any non-vm23 VM | Wrong tenant; production is vm23 (`dev`) |\n| `BOOTSTRAP.sh --stage-1` without `I_UNDERSTAND_DNS_WIPE=1` | Destructive DNS wipe |\n| Parallel SSH deploys, parallel workstation `bin/ci` suites, or broad `rcctl restart` without a named target | 1 GiB VPS; contention causes outages |\n\nWhen SSH to vm23 is required, use normal paths — but note which of them takes\n`doas` and which must not:\n\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| `doas zsh OPERATOR.sh --apply` | root, it installs `/etc` |\n| `zsh OPENBSD/bin/vps-deploy <app>` | **root** (or `dev` via passwordless doas re-exec) |\n| `zsh OPENBSD/bin/vps_ci.sh <app>` | internal child of pinned `vps-deploy`; bounded app copy-tree sync and read-only bundle check, not a test runner |\n\n`vps-deploy` runs as root. Git fetch/checkout still run as `dev` so the\n`/home/dev/pub5` tree and GitHub deploy key are never used by root. Typing the\ncommand as `dev` is fine: passwordless doas re-executes it as root.\n\n**Laws:**\n\n- Run `MASTER/bin/operator status` before starting work; the copy-paste paths\n  are in `OPENBSD/data/operator.yml`.\n- Treat `RAILS/apps.yml` and `OPENBSD/deploy_inventory.json` as inventories, not\n  suggestions.\n- Any `/etc` change made on vm23 must be copied back to `OPENBSD/mirror/etc/`.\n- Use the available compatible Ruby on OpenBSD (resolved dynamically by `OPENBSD/lib/ruby_select.sh`, which sets `$RUBY` and `$BUNDLE`). The workstation runs each selected app's `bin/ci`; vm23's `vps_ci.sh` validates the live parent lock and matching workstation proofs, refreshes the bounded app copy-tree, then checks the preinstalled production bundle.\n- Keep secrets in `/etc/*.env`; never commit them.\n- Keep Rails `config.assume_ssl = true`; do not enable `force_ssl` behind\n  relayd.\n- Prefer local checks first (`OPENBSD/bin/check`) before any SSH.\n\n**Agent dmesg (verbose file operations):** external agents (Grok CLI, Claude\nCode, Cursor) and MASTER should log mutations in OpenBSD dmesg style — terse,\nlowercase, one fact per line, path-first, e.g.:\n\n```\nwrite OPENBSD/mirror/etc/rc.d/brgen 412B +12/-3\nread MASTER/lib/reach/base.rb sha256=a1b2c3… 2048B\nrun zsh OPENBSD/bin/check-openbsd exit=0\n```\n\nName the path on every read/write/delete; show evidence on writes (diff stat or\nbyte size); show command + exit code for shell, not \"deployed successfully.\"\nSilence on success is fine for bulk checks; speak up for each mutated file.\nMASTER: `/dmesg` or `toggle dmesg` streams bus events.\n\n**Reporting** — good deploy closeout: exact host/environment, commands run,\nchecks passed/skipped/ failed, services restarted, remaining manual verification.\nBad: \"deployed\" without host/command, public health not checked, asset\nprecompile skipped after web changes, route/cert changes without relayd/acme/NSD\ncontext.\n\n## Console automation check\n\nRecovery-only expect scripts refuse to run unless a human operator exports\n`I_UNDERSTAND_CONSOLE_RISK=1` (same pattern as `I_UNDERSTAND_DNS_WIPE=1` for\n`BOOTSTRAP.sh --stage-1`).\n\n## doas.conf\n\nOpenBSD rejects `/etc/doas.conf` without a trailing newline — `doas` breaks for\neveryone. `BOOTSTRAP.sh` fixes the repo copy before install, validates `su dev -c\n'doas id'`, and rolls back on failure. No cron job installs it: the only other\npath is a deliberate `doas ksh OPENBSD/bin/validate_doas.ksh install <file> <reason>`,\nwhich validates the same way. The comment atop `etc/doas.conf` says what dev's\npasswordless rule exposes and why neither command scoping nor a password can\nnarrow it.\n\n## Backups\n\n`OPENBSD/bin/dr-pull` is the backup. It runs nightly on the operator Mac under\nlaunchd, writes a `VACUUM INTO` snapshot of every production database on vm23,\nstreams them back in one tar, checks `PRAGMA integrity_check` on arrival and\nrotates the last fourteen. `ruby OPENBSD/bin/dr-pull --check` reports the newest\npull and its age, and fails when the newest is stale — read that rather than the\nlaunchd exit status, because a snapshot that has stopped working exits 0.\n\nEach pull also records `SHA256SUMS`, taken from vm23's own `sha256` before the\nstream and compared on arrival, and copies the newest Active Storage blobs (the\ntwo-character directories beside the databases) to `~/pub5-dr/blobs/<app>`.\n`ruby OPENBSD/bin/dr-pull --drill` is the restore test: it copies the newest pull\nto a scratch directory, checks the bytes against `SHA256SUMS`, runs\n`integrity_check` on the copy, reads the migration version, table count and user\ncount, prints the seconds, and removes the scratch. Run on 2026-10-12 against\npull `20261011-0330` it restored and read back all three databases in 1.3 s\n(amber 303 users, brgen 11316, bsdports 0; integrity ok; the pull predates\n`SHA256SUMS`, so that run checked integrity only). The 11 pulls from 1 to 11\nOctober sit on the operator Mac under launchd job `no.brgen.pub4-dr`, which\nmakes the Mac the only copy off vm23.\n\n**Restored separately.** `dr-pull` holds databases and uploads, not host\nsecrets. The DNSSEC KSK/ZSK private files in `/var/nsd/zones/master` are\nirreplaceable signing material and are not currently included in the off-host\ndatabase pull. Before publishing DS records or changing any key, add these files\nto an encrypted off-host disaster-recovery set and verify a restore. Do not\ncommit them to Git or regenerate a KSK as a deployment convenience. Other\nseparate recovery inputs are `/etc/master.env`, `/etc/<app>.env`, the DKIM\nprivate key, SSH host keys and the acme-client account key. Certificates and\ntheir domain keys under `/etc/ssl` can be reissued by `acme-client` once DNS\nanswers.\n\n**Litestream replicates nothing and never has.** It is not in OpenBSD ports, so\n`pkg_add litestream` cannot install it, `/usr/local/bin/litestream` does not\nexist, and `/var/backups/litestream/` has been empty since the day it was\ncreated. It is out of `pkg_scripts` and has no `rc.d` script, so it no longer\nkeeps `rcctl ls failed` permanently non-empty. `OPENBSD/mirror/etc/litestream.yml` is\nkept because the config is correct for the day someone builds the binary from Go\nand adds an off-host bucket; its header says why the service stays off the boot\nlist.\n\nNothing on the box is a disaster-recovery replica: dr-pull's copies live on the\nMac, which is one other disk, not a bucket. An off-host object store is the\nremaining gap and it needs an account.\n\n## OpenBSD deploy\n\nUse the workstation operator for routine releases. It performs preflight, selected\nRails CI, asset builds and SHA attestation locally, then starts the pinned remote\ndeployment in tmux on vm23 and collects its transcript on the workstation.\nThe host-side `vps-deploy` is an internal deployment child, not the workstation\nentrypoint.\n\n```zsh\ncd ~/pub5\nMASTER/bin/operator vps deploy all --remote --follow\n```\n\nFor a mirror-only maintenance change, inspect the payload first with\n`doas zsh OPENBSD/OPERATOR.sh --plan`; apply and verify only the reviewed,\nscoped change. This is separate from a routine application release.\n\n**`OPENBSD/mirror/etc/` is canonical in intent, not in verified-deployability.** Diff\nbefore you install, every time:\n\n```zsh\ndiff -u /etc/relayd.conf OPENBSD/mirror/etc/relayd.conf   # read every hunk\ndoas cp -p /etc/relayd.conf /etc/relayd.conf.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)\ndoas install -o root -g wheel -m 644 OPENBSD/mirror/etc/relayd.conf /etc/relayd.conf\ndoas relayd -n -f /etc/relayd.conf                 # must print \"configuration OK\"\ndoas rcctl restart relayd\n```\n\nOn 2026-08-02 the repo copy carried `tls keypair \"bplan.pub.healthcare\"` for a\ncert that does not exist. relayd refuses to load an absent keypair, so a\nstraight repo→live copy would have taken **every** site on the box down. The two\nfiles had quietly diverged since July precisely because nobody could sync them.\n`OPENBSD/sync.rb` (see *Occasional operator tools*) is the return leg that keeps\nthis from building up.\n\nNote also that relayd's `match response header set` **overwrites** whatever the\nbackend sent, so the edge value is the only `Permissions-Policy` any browser\nsees, for every app. It has to be the union of what all backends need — a\n`geolocation=()` there silently killed brgen's `#nearby` while the Rails\ninitializer said `(self)`.\n\nWhen `bin/vps-deploy` fails, the exit trap records the failing stage in\nthe durable receipt under `/var/db/pub5/deploy_runs/`, prints\n`FAILED at stage \"<stage>\"`, attempts to restore services that were running\nbefore the release, and releases the deploy lock and resource-guard marker.\nThe durable receipt remains on vm23; the full transcript belongs to the\nworkstation collector under `~/.pub5/deployments/`. A dropped SSH session,\nsignal or failed stage is not a successful release.\n\n### The deploy sequence and its recovery\n\nRun `MASTER/bin/operator vps deploy <app|group|all> --remote` from the\nworkstation. The workstation performs the expensive and proof-producing work;\nvm23 admits, synchronizes and activates the pinned release. The flow stops at\nthe first failure.\n\n1. On the workstation, run preflight and the selected Rails apps' complete\n   `bin/ci` suites. Build production assets and record SHA attestations for\n   the same commit. The operator sends the exact preflight, CI and asset proofs\n   with the remote deployment request. No suite, dependency install, repository\n   scan or asset build runs on vm23.\n2. vm23 acquires the deploy lock, clears any caller-supplied admission token,\n   fetches and pins the exact requested SHA (or the fetched `origin/main`\n   default), and refuses a non-fast-forward update. It requires a matching\n   workstation preflight attestation; every selected Rails app also requires\n   a matching workstation CI attestation. A missing or mismatched proof is a\n   refusal before services are touched. The host does not run a fallback scan.\n3. The lock-owning parent records the original running-service snapshot in the\n   durable receipt, then checks host load, free swap and recent CPU pressure\n   before any mirror or app rollout. Fleet admission runs once; serial child\n   deploys inherit only the parent's internally established token. Resource\n   shedding remains active during the release.\n4. For `all`, apply the reviewed `OPENBSD/mirror/**` payload after admission.\n   Select the deployment order from the inventory and live service/memory\n   evidence. If the evidence is missing or degraded, move MASTER to the end.\n5. For each target, verify the checkout still matches the pinned SHA, check\n   disk and host-load limits, and run the bounded app sync plus frozen,\n   read-only production-bundle check. Verify that the staged asset manifest\n   and workstation build stamp both name the pinned SHA. A missing bundle or\n   asset is an off-host build blocker; vm23 does not install gems or compile.\n6. Prepare and migrate the production databases, restart only the selected\n   service, and verify `/up`, stylesheets, Solid Queue and the app's loopback\n   flow checks. Wait for one app to settle before touching the next. Finish\n   with the independent public canary from the workstation.\n7. On failure, the lock-owning parent restores services recorded as running\n   before the release, in serving order, one at a time. Each restore waits up\n   to `VPS_DEPLOY_RESTORE_WAIT` (240) seconds for `/up`. The receipt records\n   the stage, recovery outcome and any service that remains down. The original\n   failure exit status is preserved.\n\n#### Public release acceptance\n\nThe remote `MASTER/bin/operator vps deploy <app|group|all> --remote` path\nwaits for the pinned vm23 deploy and then runs `OPENBSD/bin/canary --public`\nfrom the workstation's independent network vantage. The collector returns a\nnonzero result if that public canary fails or cannot run; the deploy is not\naccepted as complete until the log records `post-deploy public canary (PASS)`.\nA `--detach` response means only that the tmux job was started. It is not a\nsuccessful release; follow the local deploy transcript and public-canary result.\n\nA direct invocation of `OPENBSD/bin/vps-deploy` on vm23 does not perform\nworkstation preflight, Rails test suites or asset builds. The supported path is\n`MASTER/bin/operator vps deploy <app|group|all> --remote` from the workstation;\nit supplies matching SHA attestations and runs the independent public canary.\nThe host-side `vps_ci.sh` is not a test runner: before it changes the app\ncopy-tree, it verifies the pinned SHA, workstation CI/preflight proofs and the\nparent admission token. It then performs a bounded sync and checks the\npreinstalled production bundle. After any separately\nauthorized manual or recovery operation, run `MASTER/bin/operator vps canary`\nfrom the workstation before reporting public release success. A failed public\ncanary remains a failed release assessment even when the local deploy stamp says\n`ok`. \n\n#### Interrupted deploy receipt recovery\n\nThe EXIT/HUP/INT/TERM path writes a terminal receipt after it attempts restoration.\n`SIGKILL`, a kernel crash or power loss cannot run that trap; the last atomic receipt\nremains `running` with `recovery_state=pending`. It records the exact run ID, owner\nPID and process fingerprint, pinned and previous SHAs, original running services,\nrestore order, ports, per-run log path and last durable stage.\n\nThe first rollout of this receipt protocol has one host prerequisite. `vps-deploy`\ndeliberately refuses before service control if it cannot create the durable\nreceipt. This is a one-time mirror bootstrap, not a normal release. Use only the\nexact commit already reviewed and preflighted on the workstation; do not pull an\nunpinned `origin/main`. If that exact commit cannot be established, stop before\nchanging the host. The receipt preflight runs before the normal mirror apply:\n\n```sh\n# Set this to the exact 40-character SHA already verified on the workstation.\nexport VPS_DEPLOY_SHA=\"<workstation-verified-40-character-sha>\"\ncd /home/dev/pub5\ngit fetch -q origin main\ngit merge --ff-only \"$VPS_DEPLOY_SHA\"\ndoas zsh OPENBSD/OPERATOR.sh --plan\ndoas zsh OPENBSD/OPERATOR.sh --apply\ndoas zsh OPENBSD/OPERATOR.sh --verify\n```\n\nThe bounded state and five-minute monitor view read\n`/var/db/pub5/deploy_runs/` directly. A missing, symlinked or wrongly owned\ndirectory is shown as unavailable by `vps-state` and raises a monitor alert; it\nis never treated as an empty receipt list. Re-run the reviewed\n`OPERATOR.sh --plan/--apply/--verify` sequence after updating the mirror before\nrelying on the new monitoring fields.\n\nAfter an interrupted run, inspect first:\n\n```sh\nzsh OPENBSD/bin/vps-deploy recover --plan\n```\n\nThe plan is serialized by the deploy lock and does not start, stop or restart\nservices. It reports `LIVE` when the receipt's owner fingerprint still matches,\nand `AMBIGUOUS` when a visible PID cannot be identified, another deployer process\nmay still be active, or the process-table scan fails. `RECOVERY AVAILABLE` is\nshown only when the recorded owner is gone or its PID was reused, the full service\nsnapshot is present, and no other deployer process is visible. Never apply a\n`LIVE` or `AMBIGUOUS` receipt. Copy the exact ID from a `RECOVERY AVAILABLE` row,\nreview its stage and log, then explicitly request restoration:\n\n```sh\nzsh OPENBSD/bin/vps-deploy recover --apply 20261117T010000Z-all-12345\n```\n\n`--apply` does not fetch, check out or redeploy code, and it does not roll back\ndatabase migrations or application data. It restores only services recorded as\nrunning before that run, in the saved order, then verifies brokered service state\nand each recorded app's loopback `/up` endpoint. A failed check leaves the receipt\npending and the command reports the log/daemon diagnosis path; inspect\n`/var/log/daemon` before retrying. A successful restore marks the original receipt\n`recovered` / `complete`. There is no automatic boot-time recovery and no guessed\nrelease rollback.\n\nRecovery by hand, one app at a time, waiting for each port before the next. Falcon\nneeds 30 to 40 seconds under load, and two booting together is how the apps got\nshed. Use `restart`, not `start`: `rc.d/master` runs its relayd restart, TTS warmup\nand deploy-flag removal only on restart.\n\n```zsh\ndoas rcctl restart brgen\nuntil curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:38182/up >/dev/null; do sleep 3; done\ndoas rcctl restart amber\nuntil curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:61352/up >/dev/null; do sleep 3; done\ndoas rcctl restart bsdports\nuntil curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:47312/up >/dev/null; do sleep 3; done\ndoas rcctl restart master\nuntil curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:53187/up >/dev/null; do sleep 3; done\nOPENBSD/bin/canary --local        # ports, rcctl, every public route, then each flow journey\n```\n\n`rcctl restart master` may print `kill: <pid>: No such process`. That was rc.subr's\nown wait-for-start timer, not a stale pid (the service has no pidfile); the rc.d now\nsilences that one signal. The stop path exits 0 when the process is already gone,\nkills the process group if one is left, and `rc_post` fails the stop if `:53187` is\nstill held, so a start never races a survivor. The ports above are the ones in `RAILS/apps.yml`; read them there if they change.\n\nTo deploy an exact commit, not the tip, run the workstation operator from a\nclean checkout at that commit:\n`VPS_DEPLOY_SHA=<sha> MASTER/bin/operator vps deploy all --remote`.\nDo not invoke the host-side deployer directly. A stale\n`/home/dev/.pub5-vps-deploy.lock` is reaped by the next supported run when its\nowner is gone; every exit, including a halted `all`, releases it.\n\n## Deploy-all disambiguation\n\nThe operator resolves deployment groups and app IDs from `RAILS/apps.yml`.\nGroup membership follows `deploy_root`, while `deploy_order` controls the\nserial order. MASTER belongs to its own namespace; a RAILS group request cannot\nsilently include it. The degraded order moves the MASTER namespace last.\nFour scripts read as “do everything”, and they do four different things. Pick\ndeliberately:\n\n| Script | CI | Scope | When |\n|--------|----|-------|------|\n| `ruby OPENBSD/bin/deploy [app]` | as `vps-deploy` | The one Ruby entrypoint over the same serial `vps-deploy` stages | The port's single deploy door; the zsh stages below remain the implementation |\n| `MASTER/bin/operator vps deploy <app|group|all> --remote` | **Yes** — workstation preflight and serial `bin/ci` for every selected Rails app; assets must be built and SHA-attested before SSH | Selected app, group or full fleet | Normal code release; vm23 only syncs, verifies, migrates and restarts |\n| `zsh OPENBSD/bin/vps_ci_all.sh` | **Retired refusal stub** | None | Do not use; bulk production sync is owned by the pinned `vps-deploy` parent |\n| `zsh OPENBSD/bin/deploy_all.sh` | **No** | Runs from a workstation: syncs the pub5 checkout to vm23 and runs `OPERATOR.sh`, so it reapplies `/etc`, relayd and the services, not just app code. `--per-app` also runs each `RAILS/<app>/<app>.sh` | The box's config has drifted or a fresh install needs redoing — not for shipping a code change |\n| `ksh OPENBSD/bin/start_all_apps.sh` as `dev` | **No** — recovery only | Starts every inventory app with native `rcctl`; checks all services and pins them against `resource_guard.sh` shedding | Recovery after a deliberate decision to keep every app running despite load |\n\n`vps_production_push.sh` and `manual_master_deploy.ksh` are retired refusal\nwrappers. They no longer offer a host-side fast path or manual precompile.\nUse the workstation operator command; it must complete local tests before SSH.\nThe asset archive must also be transferred and attested for the pinned SHA;\nvm23 refuses deployment when it is missing. `deploy_all.sh` is the wider\nconfiguration operation, not a routine code deploy.\n\n## Occasional operator tools\n\nNothing in the repo calls these — they are run by hand, which is exactly why\nthey need to be listed somewhere. An orphan script is indistinguishable from a\ndead one until it is written down.\n\n| Script | Run from | What it is for |\n|--------|----------|----------------|\n| `ruby OPENBSD/sync.rb` (as `doas ruby`) | vm23 | Mirror live `/etc` config **back into** `OPENBSD/`, with secret redaction. The repo→live direction is well travelled; this is the return leg, and skipping it is how `relayd.conf` drifted for weeks (see the warning under *OpenBSD deploy*). |\n| `ruby OPENBSD/ptr_openbsd_amsterdam.rb --ipv4 … --hostname …` | anywhere | Set the PTR record via openbsd.amsterdam's `ptr4`/`ptr6` endpoints; `--ipv6` sets the v6 record. Needed only if the VM's IP changes. It prints the request as a dry run unless `APPLY_PTR=1` is set. |\n| `zsh OPENBSD/bin/vps_run_remote.sh` | workstation | Bootstrap a *fresh* VM: copies `vps_install_all.sh` up through the server4 hypervisor jump and runs it. Not for routine deploys — use `vps-deploy`. |\n| `ksh OPENBSD/bin/manual_master_deploy.ksh` | retired | Refuses; vm23 does not kill processes or compile production assets |\n| `sh OPENBSD/bin/amber_queue_sweep.sh [APP]` | vm23 | **Deletes** finished jobs, orphaned executions, unfinished Turbo broadcasts and duplicate media jobs from a Solid Queue backlog (amber by default); drain-jobs.sh runs due jobs, this removes what should never run. Named in `RAILS/amber/README.md` |\n| `zsh OPENBSD/bin/deploy-diff.sh` | workstation | Read-only: runs `config_drift_check.rb --remote`, then diffs `relayd.conf` (which the check excludes) and prints `rcctl check`. It changes nothing in either direction; `sync.rb` above is what pulls the live side back into the repo. |\n| `sh OPENBSD/bin/amber_queue_sweep.sh [APP]` | vm23 | Delete a stale Solid Queue backlog (finished jobs, orphaned executions, unfinished Turbo broadcasts, duplicate media jobs) with sqlite3, no Rails boot. `drain-jobs.sh` runs due jobs hourly; this removes what should never run. |\n\n## Self-healing cron (vm23)\n\nTracked mirror: `OPENBSD/data/root.crontab` (installed idempotently by\n`OPERATOR.sh`).
